title: Jonah and the Trail
premise: Petra Vasquez chases storms for salvage money she never keeps, because the crew of the Optimist's Wake — cheerful, patient creditors — always find her. When an upriver expedition goes silent, its last radio call names her as the only pilot who knows the flooded canyon route. Hired by the expedition's estranged daughter to beat a rival salvage fleet, Petra races six tides toward the wreck of the Meridian Star, where the truth about her missing brother and the debt that owns her are tangled together. She wins the race but chooses justice over salvage: she sinks the evidence that would have made her rich, exposes the fleet's sabotage, and finally stops running — because her found crew is worth standing still for.
about_author: Ines Kavanagh is a former river guide who spent five seasons on the flood-country waterways that inspired this novel. She writes adventure stories about people who owe too much and love anyway.

chapters.title: Debt Weather
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Chasing a storm across the salt flats, she salvages just enough to make a payment — then the Optimist's Wake crew finds her at a fuel dock, smiling, raising her interest. Emotional beat: exhaustion disguised as competence; establish that stopping costs more than moving.

chapters.title: The Silence Upstream
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A garbled radio transmission from the lost Meridian expedition names her by name before cutting out. The speaker's daughter, Noor Haddad, tracks Petra down with an offer: pilot her upriver, beat the salvage fleet, split whatever they find. Beat: reluctant hook — Petra recognizes the canyon route as one only her brother ever mapped.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Petra and Noor's POV alternating. They load the boat and learn the rival fleet, led by the charming Voss, has already bought the harbor master. The tide tables give them six windows; the fleet needs only four. Beat: dread sharpening into resolve as Petra commits to the run.

chapters.title: The Canyon That Drowns Twice a Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. First tide window: a white-knuckle passage through the flooded gorge, where her brother's hand-painted markers still cling to the walls. Noor proves braver and stranger than expected. Beat: first trust between them, earned in spray and near-death.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Left Behind
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They discover a sabotaged expedition camp — cut lines, drained tanks — proof the fleet didn't just race the Meridian crew, it killed them. Beat: grief curdling into purpose; the mission changes from salvage to reckoning.

chapters.title: The Man Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Voss corners them at a midriver trading post, offers to buy out Petra's debt in exchange for abandoning Noor. He knows about her brother. Beat: temptation laid bare — Petra realizes the Wake and the fleet may be the same animal wearing different faces.

chapters.title: Brother Water
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, with Petra's confession inside it. Petra reveals her brother mapped the route for the Meridian expedition and vanished with it; the wreck may hold his last log. Beat: identity crisis — she has been running from the answer for three years.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The fleet ambushes them in the narrows; Noor is taken, the boat holed. Petra survives by doing the thing she swore off: asking for help, from river people who remember her brother fondly. Beat: found family crystallizes — strangers become crew.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian Star
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Final tide window: she dives the wreck alone, finds her brother's log proving the fleet sank the Meridian deliberately — and finds no body, meaning he may have walked away. She surfaces to Voss's guns and Noor's rescue party. Beat: climax — she chooses to broadcast the log on open channels rather than trade it for her freedom.

chapters.title: Still Water
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The broadcast burns the fleet; Voss is arrested by the river authority he'd bribed too cheaply. Petra's debt dies with the Wake's exposed ledgers. Her brother sends a postcard from downcoast — alive, not ready, but reachable. Beat: resolution — Petra moors the boat, unpacks her bags, and stays.
